business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Magazine Publishing and Sponsored Media Placements

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Korea Free Trade Agreement (KORUS FTA), signed June 30, 2007, entered into force March 15, 2012

Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investments, signed September 12, 2007, entered into force December 1, 2008

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Report and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended) together with its Presidential Enforcement Decree and Financial Services Commission regulations; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment; Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 590, as amended), Articles 19, 23 and 54 regarding corporate names and share registers; Real Name Financial Transactions Act; and the Financial Intelligence Unit's Guidance on Customer Identification and Beneficial Ownership Identification. There is no public UBO register in Korea; beneficial ownership information is collected by the Financial Intelligence Unit and relevant supervisory authorities during inspections and is not published.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Registration / Certificate of Existence (Legal Entity Registration Certificate issued by the court registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Option A: Notarize the Korean original at a Korean notary public, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for submission in any Hague Apostille Convention state. Option B: For a non-Convention state, the notarized original must be authenticated by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the consular section of the destination country in Korea; the two routes are mutually exclusive and must never be applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Confirmation of Current Corporate Status (excerpt from the corporate register showing no dissolution or liquidation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean District Court Registry Office or Supreme Court Registration Office (I-ONE portal)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Option A: Have the certificate notarized and then certified with an Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Hague Convention destination. Option B: For non-Convention countries, after notarization obtain MOFA authentication and consular legalization of the destination state in Korea; do not chain Apostille and consular legalization on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (approving the formation and appointing the local registered agent and law firm representative)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company board of directors (corporation in formation/promoters) and the engaged Korean law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Option A: Notarize the signed Korean text and attach a certified English translation; apply to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for an Apostille if the destination is an Apostille Convention member. Option B: If the destination is not a member, use the consular legalization channel only, consisting of MOFA authentication followed by legalization at the destination consulate; no mixed procedure is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Statutes of the Yuhan Hoesa), including name, capital, business scope, and director details
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarized by a Korean notary public and issued by the incorporators/attorneys
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Option A: For Apostille states, apostillize the notarized Articles through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs after notarization. Option B: For non-Apostille states, the notarized Articles must undergo MOFA authentication and then destination-consulate legalization; the parallel route requirement is absolute and both routes are never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (showing banking relationship history and no adverse AML events, issued by the company's opening or reference bank in Korea)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank relationship manager or foreign correspondent bank branch in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Option A: Have the bank's authorized signatory notarize the letter, then apostillize with the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for use in Apostille Convention jurisdictions. Option B: For non-Convention jurisdictions, the notarized bank letter must be sent to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for authentication and then to the destination state's consulate for legalization; these are alternative, exclusive routes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Perform mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, signatories, and commercial counterparties against: (1) the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's designated persons list and the Korean Financial Services Commission's administrative sanction database; (2) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (3) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists; (4) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (5) UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list; and (6) LexisNexis or World-Check adverse media and politically exposed person (PEP) profiles. Apply a 25% ownership threshold and control test, requiring enhanced due diligence for foreign public officials, their family members and close associates. Update screening at least once every 90 days, and record all results in the AML file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: I-ONE (Internet Registry Service) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea; official registration portal for corporate name search, reservation, and incorporation filing (www.i-one.kr); supplementary business registration and tax identification requires Hometax (National Tax Service online portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Commercial Act of Korea requires the company name to be recorded in Korean (Hangul). A foreign-language name may be used as a trade name only after the Korean legal name is registered, and any non-Korean name must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul for registration. The four-tier convention accepted by the registry is: (1) distinctive brand or trade name; (2) subject matter describing the digital publishing and media business; (3) the Korean limited liability suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'; and (4) an identifying number or territorial element only if required to differentiate the name from an existing identical mark. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any pre-existing registered company, and must not imply public authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the I-ONE registry, the applicant must, within 14 days of rejection, file a written administrative objection with the Chief Judge of the relevant District Court Registration Office using the formal name-use objection form. Attach a clear printout of the proposed Hangul transliteration, a copy of the refusal notice, a full explanation of why the name is not confusingly similar to any existing registered names, and the intended proof of use of the foreign trade name. Where the refusal is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, file a prior ministerial approval application from the relevant ministry (e.g., Financial Services Commission or Ministry of Justice) and resubmit the application. Judicial appeal under Article 84 of the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act remains available if the administrative objection is denied.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a low-risk digital magazine publishing LLC, Korean tax authorities and banks generally accept a registered agent or licensed serviced office as the statutory registered office, but the National Tax Service may challenge a purely virtual commercial mailbox if no supporting administrative substance exists. Banks opening corporate accounts typically require physical verification, a lease agreement in the company's name, and at least one director present at the bank. A virtual office without a real meeting room is likely to be rejected by major commercial banks for the purpose of opening an operating account and receiving AdSense or Stripe payouts. A serviced office with lease agreement, reception, meeting space, and a local contact person is advisable to maintain tax-resident substance and banking functionality.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection likelihood is low but real: estimated 10-15% probability in the first year for a low-risk digital publisher with no statutory license; likelihood rises to approximately 25-30% if the company claims frequent VAT refunds, uses a virtual office, or lists an address shared with many other incorporated entities. Inspection checklist: physical name plate at registered office; original lease agreement and rent payment evidence; corporate record book, minute book, and seals kept in Korea; director's identity and employment evidence; bank statements and business invoices retained on site; no unauthorized residential mailbox only; clear separation from any other entity's address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed tariff under the Local Tax Act and Court Registration Fee Regulation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal statutory fee for name search; no market or attorney premium included.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Notary Public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean Notary Fee Act schedule and MOFA official fee tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance subcontractor / licensed KYC data provider engaged by the law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market per-screening benchmark for continuous global data feeds, not a percentage of capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent service provider in Seoul
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market annual fee for a serviced office with meeting space for non-license-required digital media companies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff or attorney facilitation fee; not a government fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page market rate for legal translation, including affidavit of translation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), Articles 601 et seq.; Commercial Registration Act (as amended); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for non-resident capital subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Civil Affairs Department, Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (Court Registry Office), with electronic filings accepted through the Internet Registration Office (IREGIS) of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), submitted with executed Articles of Incorporation and all statutory annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa. The articles of incorporation must state a fixed capital amount and the class and value of each member's contribution. Cash consideration must be fully deposited into a provisional corporate bank account in the company's name before the court filing, and contribution-in-kind must be reported and examined by a court-appointed inspector where required. The deposited funds are not state escrow but are blocked for the company's exclusive use until incorporation is registered; withdrawal before registration is a disqualifying defect. The United States dollar fee shown assumes illustrative paid-in capital of KRW 10,000,000 and includes registration tax, local education surtax and court fee; actual fees are calculated on the registered capital amount.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF KR_YUHANGHOESA, A YUHAN HOESA TO BE INCORPORATED UNDER THE LAWS OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The undersigned incorporating members and the persons designated to act as the initial director or directors of the company, acting unanimously in lieu of a formal meeting pursuant to the articles of incorporation and the Korean Commercial Act, adopt the following resolutions. WHEREAS the company has been formed as a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) for the business of digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements, whose registered office and principal place of business shall be adopted by this resolution; WHEREAS the articles of incorporation have been executed by all members, capital contributions have been subscribed, and the amount of capital is stated therein; and WHEREAS the corresponding statutory officers have been identified to manage the company and to perform all statutory functions upon incorporation registration. NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS. 1. Share Capital Subscription. It is resolved that the subscription to the share capital is hereby ratified; that all capital contributions, whether cash or non-cash property, have been lawfully allocated among the members in accordance with the articles of incorporation; and that any contribution not paid at the date of this resolution shall be treated as a lawful receivable of the company until fully performed. 2. Registered Office. It is resolved that the registered office shall be [Address, South Korea]; that the company may change its registered office by member resolution; and that the representative director shall cause all registry and tax notices to be updated accordingly. 3. Banking Authorization

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) - HomeTax System (hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS) for export declaration processing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) is a domestic corporation for tax purposes. Within 20 days of commencing the digital publishing business, the legal representative must apply for business registration through the HomeTax system at the competent district tax office; required documents include the certificate of corporate registration, the company's articles of incorporation, foreign shareholder identity and foreign capital reporting documents (if any), and the executed business premises lease or ownership proof. Upon approval, the NTS issues a Business Registration Certificate (business registration number) that serves as the unified TIN for corporate income tax and VAT. For a foreign non-resident supplier without a Korean place of business that supplies electronic/digital services to Korean consumers, a separate simplified foreign business VAT registration must be made via HomeTax, and the foreign supplier is required to appoint a Korean tax representative under the Framework Act for National Taxes. Procurement of the TIN is not subject to minimum capital; a physical address for the deemed Korean place of business must be established.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea has no check-the-box election. A Yuhan Hoesa is taxed as a corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act; no pass-through or hybrid-entity election is available. Group taxation is separate and does not alter entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold for a Yuhan Hoesa corporation; every corporate business must register for VAT. A KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover threshold applies only to simplified-taxable individual entrepreneurs, not to a Yuhan Hoesa. Foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic services to Korean consumers are required to register for VAT if their annual Korean electronic-service supplies exceed KRW 10,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All corporate VAT taxpayers must issue and submit electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system for B2B supplies. Submission is not a real-time fiscal clearance; the NTS processes and reconciles invoice data using its integrated API/EDI interface, and no anti-fraud stamping or pre-approval is required. For B2C digital magazine subscriptions and AdSense payouts, a cash receipt may be requested by the consumer; electronic tax invoices are mandatory for B2B sales and must be reported in the VAT return. Failure to transmit through HomeTax exposes the taxpayer to statutory penalty tax and interface rejection penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, export of goods and services supplied to foreign countries is zero-rated. For the digital magazine portal, digital subscription and advertising receipts qualify for 0% VAT only where the recipient is a non-resident or foreign entity, the place of supply is outside Korea, the service is effectively consumed abroad, and the export proceeds are received in foreign currency from abroad. If the digital advertising or sponsorship service is deemed to be consumed in Korea or to serve a domestic advertiser, the general 10% VAT applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration (Export Declaration) via UNI-PASS and the customs export clearance certificate for any physical promotional or fulfilment goods accompanying the digital publishing service

Signed digital service export contract, purchase order, or written agreement with the foreign counterparty, together with itemised commercial invoices identifying the foreign end-user and service period
Foreign-exchange receipt confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, evidencing that the export or supply payments were received from abroad within the statutory settlement period

Bill of lading or air waybill when physical goods are exported; for pure digital services, a digital delivery report or metrics report showing the foreign IP or customer location may be substituted for transport documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, the NTS and Korea Customs Service will verify the export declaration, place-of-supply, customer tax and foreign-residence status, payment flow, and repatriation within 180 days. Missing, inconsistent, or fraudulent export evidence leads to reversal of the zero-rating, reassessment of 10% VAT, statutory additional taxes for underreporting/unpaid tax, and daily delinquency charges; deliberate false documentation may additionally be prosecuted under the Act on Punishment of Tax Evaders, with criminal fines/imprisonment and retrospective clawback of VAT credits and refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank and operator of the Foreign Exchange Information System, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance serving as the principal foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberal current account convertibility framework but reserves prior-approval and reporting obligations that companies must satisfy. Capital account transactions are subject to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, which requires foreign direct investment, inbound equity capital contributions, non-resident subscriptions, and repatriation of proceeds to be reported through designated foreign exchange banks or, in certain circumstances, to the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The KRW is convertible for ordinary business transactions; dividends, service fees, and trade settlements can be remitted provided the underlying transaction is evidenced and the borrowing or investment was reported. Nevertheless, the Financial Transaction Reports Act, the BOK's Foreign Exchange Information System, and the Know Your Customer obligations of domestic banks create practical friction for rapid cross-border movements. Profit remittance hurdles are manageable but require an audited financial statement, tax clearance, and a certified foreign exchange transaction report. Surrender requirements are not applied as a blanket 100% conversion; however, exporters must bring proceeds into Korea within statutory deadlines and may retain balances in authorized foreign currency accounts. The system is therefore liberal with supervision, not a strict control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and BOK regulations, export receipts must be collected through a domestic foreign exchange bank and settled within 90 days of the export declaration date. The exporter may hold foreign currency in an authorized foreign currency account without mandatory immediate conversion into KRW, but upon settlement into Korean won, the exchange bank must report the transaction electronically through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Extensions are possible for projects with long payment cycles or construction/installment contracts, subject to prior bank or BOK approval depending on the amount.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise or Revolut Business are not authorized by the Financial Services Commission or the Bank of Korea as domestic foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. They can neither issue Korean IBANs nor act as settlement banks for KRW or foreign currency capital accounts. For a Yuhan Hoesa, using a fintech EMI would fail regulatory KYC and undermine the ability to receive foreign investment registration and capital verification certificates. Local tier-1 commercial banks are mandatory at account opening; EMIs can only be auxiliary for low-value expense cards if accepted by local partners, but never for treasury flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory. At least one statutory director or a properly authorized representative with a valid passport, corporate seal certificate, and board resolution must appear in person at a domestic branch of the chosen tier-1 bank to sign banking agreements and undergo face-to-face KYC. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for non-resident directors; however, a local branch may permit a power-of-attorney arrangement after an in-person interview has been completed by the director, subject to bank discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border ownership structure with 25% or more non-resident shareholding and opaque beneficial ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an organizational chart, the corporate business registration certificate, passport copies of all shareholders, a shareholder register, a UBO declaration form, and a sworn affidavit detailing the source of wealth and source of funds for the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital media and publishing revenue streams that appear through payment service providers without clear licensing or royalty contracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit content licensing agreements, platform payout statements from Stripe and AdSense, sponsor/advertiser contracts, sample invoices and settlement reports, and a written explanation of the ISIC 5813 commercial model with exact revenue classifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually rapid or high-frequency international payment velocity to advertisements, content syndication partners, and affiliate networks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply a CRM disbursement ledger, vendor contracts, a board-approved treasury policy, monthly clearing reports, and a payment reconciliation matrix mapping each outbound wire to an underlying contractual obligation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement mismatch where Stripe or AdSense funds arrive from a PSP instead of the actual advertiser or subscriber.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide PSP settlement reports matching individual transaction lines, database subscription analytics, chargeback history, customer email verification logs, and a completed AML questionnaire demonstrating that the PSP is an independent payment intermediary rather than a hidden beneficial owner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection for a Yuhan Hoesa must be routed as SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's account to the domestic capital escrow account at a designated foreign exchange bank. The payment must cite the Foreign Exchange Information System purpose code for foreign direct investment and be accompanied by the business license, shareholder resolution, capital contribution plan, and the company corporate certificate. Within 30 days of receipt, the company must submit a declaration of foreign direct investment and obtain a foreign exchange bank certificate to support the CPA-issued capital verification report. Pending verification, KRW operational expenditures may only be funded from paid-in capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for advertising, content licensing, server hosting, and foreign affiliate fees should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 direct transfers from the operating account. Large negotiated rights acquisitions may use commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT710) or documentary collections to secure performance. Each outbound payment must be supported by a contract, invoice, tax invoice, prior FX transaction report, and the relevant payment purpose code. For related-party digital ecosystem payees, an intercompany transfer pricing or authorization statement is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Contractual forward currency exchange contracts with a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-KRW offshore currency exposures, subject to BOK reporting
Currency swaps for medium-term hedging of foreign borrowings, subject to derivative eligibility and BOK reporting
Plain vanilla foreign exchange options when supported by documented commercial or investment exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Payment (corporation tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December fiscal year-end, on or before March 31 immediately after the close of the year; for non-calendar fiscal years, within three months from the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% non-filing additional tax on unpaid taxable amount; 10% under-reporting additional tax (20% for gross negligence); statutory daily late-payment surcharge from the due date; continued default results in tax seizure, credit freeze, and cancellation of business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Return and Payment (local corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government authority of the registered office jurisdiction (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government or respective city/province tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the national corporate income tax return deadline; for a calendar year-end, normally no later than April 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the payable local tax, under-reporting penalty of 10% to 20%, monthly/statutory late-payment surcharge, and local administrative compulsory collection leading to seizure of bank accounts and corporate property.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary meeting approval of financial statements and appropriation of profits or disposition of losses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members/quota-holders of the Yuhan Hoesa; statutory auditor where appointed; tax copy attached to the corporate tax return filed with the NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared within 42 days after fiscal year-end and laid before an ordinary general meeting within the 3-month statutory period; for a calendar year, approval by March 31 and CIT filing by the same date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting or approve annual statements exposes officers to commercial-code administrative fines (up to KRW 5 million per instance), makes contested distributions void, and undermines verifiable accounting for tax audits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recurring VAT return filings (preliminary and final value-added tax returns for digital publishing income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (VAT desk, HomeTax system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year: preliminary Jan-Mar by April 25; first-half final by July 25; preliminary Jul-Sep by October 25; second-half final by January 25 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT non-filing/under-reporting surtax of 10% to 20% of the deficient amount plus daily late-payment interest; serious repeated defaults can trigger trading VAT registration cancellation and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Annual Report (mandatory only if the Yuhan Hoesa has a foreign investment holding 10% or more, or receives foreign-investment cash/equity recognition)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) through the foreign investment support portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 following the fiscal year-end; a shareholding transfer or capital change by a foreign investor must additionally be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the foreign-investment annual report may void tax incentives, attract an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and impair the foreign investor's recognition for exchange-control and dividend repatriation purposes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its enforcement decree, a Yuhan Hoesa/LLC must appoint an independent certified public accountant if its total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.5 million). Mandatory external audit is also required if the company is listed, publicly offered, a financial institution, or has been designated by the Financial Services Commission for public-interest reasons. Korean law contains no separate turnover or employee-count audit threshold; if the balance-sheet asset test is not met, an otherwise unlisted digital media LLC is exempt from statutory audit unless designation applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies, financial institutions and designated large corporations; unlisted companies may adopt K-IFRS voluntarily or prepare financial statements under Korean GAAP (K-GAAP); eligible SMEs may use the SME Accounting Standards. Audited entities must present comparative financial statements and follow the Financial Services Commission's external audit instruction.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea has no separate annual UBO confirmation form for a Yuhan Hoesa; the beneficial ownership chain is maintained through the company's member/quota-holder register. A share or quota transfer becomes effective against the company only when entered in the Register of Members; the company must update the register promptly upon notification and within the 30-day statutory change-reporting window when the transfer involves a foreign investor or alters filed foreign-investment data. If foreign-invested, the company files an annual foreign-investment report confirming the ultimate beneficial owners and their Korean holding percentages. For domestic-only shareholders, annual UBO confirmation is achieved by maintenance of accurate on-site registers and inclusion of shareholder information in corporate tax filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors / executive quota-holder action register
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Collateral / lien records
Minute Book of ordinary general meetings and management resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 1,000 per year for professional registered-office/registered-agent legal address services in Seoul or a provincial commercial city.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 per year for a certified audit of a mid-size or moderate revenue digital publishing entity; larger K-IFRS audits with group consolidations may exceed USD 25,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% above KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Digital magazine and online media operations in Korea do not enjoy a freestanding patent box, but the Restriction of Special Taxation Act permits R&D and manpower tax credits for qualifying software, platform technology, and digital publishing development; foreign-invested high-technology enterprises in Free Economic Zones may obtain 100% corporate income tax exemption for 5 years and a 50% exemption for the following 2 years under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; incremental job creation credits and capital investment credits are also available

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Payable Return as filed by a domestic Yuhan Hoesa through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus an interim preliminary return for the first six months of the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a December 31 fiscal year end, the annual corporate income tax return is due by March 31 of the following year; the interim preliminary return is due by the last day of the second month following the first six months, which is August 31

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, business registration number, registered address, fiscal year, and tax-reporting status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation and therefore taxable on worldwide income; non-resident shareholders and their shareholding percentages must be fully disclosed in the stock ownership schedule; any misclassification as a mere Korean permanent establishment of a foreign principal will trigger aggressive NTS audit and reassessment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet schedule and supporting financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all Stripe settlement reports, AdSense payout statements, and sponsored media placement invoices to gross receipts; do not net payment gateway commissions or agency fees unless a separate arm's-length service invoice exists; unreconciled foreign payment-rail inflows are a fatal red flag

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement and accounting profit before corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All digital magazine subscriptions, advertising revenue, affiliate revenue, sponsored content, and platform royalties must be accrued in the Korean LLC; routing any portion of revenue to a personal foreign bank account, a non-resident shell, or an undisclosed crypto wallet is criminal tax evasion

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation schedule: non-deductible expenses and statutory add-backs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible entertainment expenses, unlawful political donations, excessive interest paid to non-resident related parties under Korean thin-capitalization rules, and non-arm's-length royalties; a non-resident investor cannot strip Korean digital profits through management fees without documentary substance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before loss carryforward and non-taxable income deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply prior-year tax losses strictly within the limited carryforward period; a foreign parent cannot use overseas losses to offset Korean LLC profits; digital platform losses must be supported by audited Korean books

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base and graduated corporate tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%, 19%, and 21% brackets in the legally prescribed stacking order; the domestic Korean LLC is a worldwide taxpayer; the existence of foreign shareholders does not convert Korea's entity-level taxation into a pass-through regime

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credit, alternative minimum tax, and incentive claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only statutory R&D credits, job creation credits, foreign investment credits, and foreign taxes paid actually creditable under the Corporate Tax Act; do not double-claim administrative incentives with DTA benefits; the foreign shareholder cannot personally claim Korean entity tax credits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interim tax prepayments and other tax withholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry forward interim return payments and amounts withheld from interest or dividend income; if the foreign parent has a Korean permanent establishment through the digital magazine portal, further income attribution and crediting rules must be reconciled in this box

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction and transfer-pricing disclosure schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every intercompany royalty, digital advertising technology fee, content licensing fee, management service charge, and intra-group financing transaction; state the transfer-pricing method, comparability factors, and arm's-length range; failing to file the Local File or Master File at the statutory threshold allows the NTS to apply a discretionary adjustment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident distribution schedule, dividend withholding, and DTA beneficial ownership declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all actual and constructive distributions to non-resident shareholders; calculate the 22% statutory dividend withholding tax or the applicable treaty-reduced rate; attach the Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership certificate, and economic substance evidence; absent such documents, the payor may be held liable for the full withholding tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an addition to tax of 10% of the unpaid tax; an unfounded or incorrect filing triggers 20% of the unpaid tax, rising to 30% for fraudulent concealment; unpaid tax bears a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022%; criminal tax evasion under the Korean Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine not exceeding 5 times the evaded tax, in addition to civil restitution and full reassessment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate, comprising a 20% dividend withholding tax plus a 10% local income tax surtax on the 20% tax, applied to outbound dividends paid by the Korean Yuhan Hoesa to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate from the competent authority of its residence country, provide a signed beneficial ownership certificate, evidence share ownership and holding period, and submit a treaty-relief application through the Korean withholding agent before the distribution date; the withholding agent then files the reduced-rate withholding tax return through HomeTax; if the full 22% is withheld, the non-resident may apply for a refund with the National Tax Service, but this does not waive substantive economic substance requirements, and OECD limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose test clauses may deny relief where no genuine business activity exists
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalty payments to non-resident related parties carry a statutory 22% withholding tax; applicable tax treaties may reduce interest and royalties to 0%, 10%, or 15%, and certain competitor-based treaties exempt interest; any excess fee above an arm's-length amount is recharacterized as a constructive dividend and remains fully subject to 22% withholding or treaty reduction only if beneficial ownership is proven

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion trigger the Korean Local File requirement; related-party transactions exceeding KRW 50 billion combined with group revenue above KRW 100 billion trigger the Master File requirement; a Country-by-Country report is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above KRW 100 billion
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations directly, but the doctrine of substance over form is embedded in the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and the National Tax Basic Act; the National Tax Service will scrutinize Core Income-Generating Activities and will disregard an entity lacking real personnel, premises, decision-making, IP ownership, and risk-taking when deciding DTA beneficial ownership and Korean permanent establishment exposure; a pure shell intermediary is treated as fiscally transparent and all income is reattributed to the Korean LLC or the ultimate non-resident principal

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Direct Tax Evasion and Cyber Revenue Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean digital magazine LLC receives Stripe, AdSense, and sponsored-media payments but intentionally diverts substantial revenue to a personal overseas account, undisclosed foreign payment stack, or cryptocurrency wallet; false invoices are issued and less than 20% of actual gross receipts are reported to the NTS
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Korean Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the tax evaded; the Framework Act for National Taxes also imposes a 20% understatement penalty, increased to 30% for concealment, plus 0.022% daily late-payment surcharges and full reassessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director or beneficial owner who controls the diversion is personally liable under the secondary tax obligation doctrine of the National Tax Collection Act, allowing the NTS to seize personal assets, attach Korean bank accounts, and impose an overseas departure restriction or travel ban where delinquent tax exceeds KRW 50 million; criminal imprisonment is personal and cannot be discharged by corporate liquidation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud, Shell Company Abuse, and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC pays royalties or management fees of 80% of gross profit to a foreign holding company with no employees, no servers, no research and development, no decision-making authority, no real IP assignment, and no Core Income-Generating Activities; the Local File and Master File are not prepared despite the statutory transaction threshold, and no arm's-length benchmarking exists
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 4 and 21 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the NTS may disregard the shell parent, recharacterize excessive royalty payments as constructive dividends, adjust the taxable income on an arm's-length range, and impose penalty tax on the corrected income; failure to submit transfer-pricing documentation further permits evidentiary presumption and denial of internal comparables
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign sham agreements and knowingly allow profit stripping can be jointly and severally liable for the assessed corporate tax, interest, and penalties as officers actually managing the business; chronic delinquent status leads to blacklisting, travel bans, and seizure of personal property; fraudulent transfer or false documentation may trigger imprisonment under the Special Economic Crimes Act, with terms up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Foreign Exchange Violation, and Payment-Rail Misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC settles digital magazine advertising revenue through unregistered non-resident payment intermediaries and receives final proceeds in offshore bank or crypto accounts without filing foreign exchange reports with the Bank of Korea; ultimate beneficial ownership information for non-resident shareholders is hidden and the true payment source is obscured to defeat AML monitoring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information impose criminal penalties of imprisonment up to 3 to 5 years and fines of up to KRW 500 million; the NTS and Financial Services Commission may also impose administrative fines, freeze accounts, and disallow all associated expenses for Korean corporate tax purposes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who directs unregistered outward remittances faces personal monetary fines, freezing of personal assets, passport revocation, and travel restrictions; civil restitution of the unlawfully transferred foreign exchange may be ordered; if the corporate form is used only as a facade for personal payment-rail laundering, the court will pierce the corporate veil and impose imprisonment directly on the director
